title: Picture characters and changing communication
instructions: Read the five-paragraph text. Match paragraphs A–E to the same shared list of headings A–H; use a heading at most once. Answer the remaining view and summary questions. This is a shorter preparatory set, not a full IELTS Reading section.

stimulus.text:
A. Picture characters have become a prominent part of online messages. The account places their global expansion in the early 2010s, followed within a few years by very widespread use. Their cultural visibility was reflected when a dictionary organisation selected a laughing-face symbol as its word of the year. Such selections represent the concerns or mood of a particular period. They can also become dated as that period passes. The interesting question is therefore not simply how popular a particular symbol is, but what its rise reveals about changes in human communication.

B. Language changes partly because relationships and identities change. Different generations and social groups adapt expression to reflect who they are. New concepts also need a way to be communicated. Words are continually created for these purposes, but picture characters add something beyond another set of vocabulary items. They supply a different expressive system alongside words. Their development therefore belongs to a broader story about people responding to changing social needs, rather than an isolated story about decoration on a telephone screen.

C. The technology through which a message travels can reshape the message itself. On a small phone screen, a brief written exchange may lack the expression or tone available in a face-to-face or spoken conversation. A picture character can help restore that emotional framing. A smile beside a short sentence can signal warmth that the words alone might not clearly convey. This explanation concerns what the system offers in a particular communication setting; it does not require the claim that written language has become unnecessary.

D. There is also a striking contrast with earlier communication tools. A person might once have replaced a landline telephone to obtain a new feature without having to update the language used through it. Picture characters, however, are redesigned and expanded as phones and operating systems change. Their available forms are therefore linked to products that undergo repeated updates. The argument treats this continuing replacement as a limitation on their usefulness, while also recognising that technological change encourages creativity in how people use them.

E. Picture characters now reach into activities beyond private conversation. The account connects them with advertising, politics, fashion, art and entertainment. Their appearance in so many settings makes them a useful subject for understanding contemporary life. Examining why people adopt them and how they function can reveal more than a fact about vocabulary. It can help explain the relationship between communication, technology and society. The argument ultimately uses a familiar small symbol to open a much larger question about people and the world around them.

teachingAnchors.label: Test the whole paragraph
teachingAnchors.text: Read each paragraph fully and state its central claim before looking at headings. A first sentence may introduce a contrast rather than the final point. In the course-book city example, an opening about an extreme northern location is followed by a discussion of unusual rules: a location-only heading misses that change in focus. Apply the same test here to popularity, emotional meaning, product updates and society.

teachingAnchors.label: Challenge the qualifier
teachingAnchors.text: Compare the scope of each heading with the paragraph. All, only, always and every can turn a partly relevant option into an unsupported claim. Headings often paraphrase rather than repeat nouns. Match main argument to main argument, not one example to a broad label. Use each heading at most once; there are three unused distractors.

teachingAnchors.label: Separate claim and evidence
teachingAnchors.text: A writer-view answer needs the author’s position, not a fact you believe outside the passage. YES agrees, NO contradicts and NOT GIVEN is not established either way. For summary completion, locate the relevant paragraph and keep the one-word grammatical fit. Finish independently, then explain a rejected heading and a scope error after submission.

criteria.label: Textual evidence
criteria.description: Use only the stated text, respect scope and word limits, and distinguish contradiction from insufficient information.

assessment.feedbackGuidance: After submission, state each paragraph’s main claim before discussing the heading. Identify a distractor that repeats the subject but changes the relationship or scope. In the city teaching example, northern location is introductory while unusual regulation is the paragraph’s focus; a topic word is not the whole argument. For YES/NO/NOT GIVEN use the writer’s actual position, and distinguish uncertainty about cause from denial of an observed change. For summary completion copy one exact word with grammatical fit. Revise one gist statement and explain one rejected qualifier. Raw accuracy only; no band.

locale.instructionsFa: متن پنج‌بندی را بخوانید. هر بند را به یک عنوان از فهرست مشترک A تا H وصل کنید؛ هر عنوان حداکثر یک بار به کار می‌رود. سپس پرسش دیدگاه و خلاصه را پاسخ دهید. این مجموعه بخش کامل آزمون نیست.

teachingAnchorsFa.label: موضوع کل بند
teachingAnchorsFa.text: کل بند را بخوانید و ادعای اصلی را مشخص کنید. در نمونهٔ شهرِ کتاب آموزشی، جملهٔ آغازین از موقعیت بسیار شمالی می‌گوید اما ادامه مقررات غیرعادی را توضیح می‌دهد؛ عنوان صرفاً جغرافیایی کافی نیست. همین روش را برای محبوبیت، احساس، به‌روزرسانی محصول و جامعه به کار ببرید.

teachingAnchorsFa.label: حد عنوان
teachingAnchorsFa.text: همه، فقط، همیشه و هر می‌توانند عنوانی ظاهراً مرتبط را نادرست کنند. عنوان معمولاً بازگویی است، نه تکرار اسم‌ها. هر عنوان را حداکثر یک بار استفاده کنید؛ سه عنوان اضافه وجود دارد.

teachingAnchorsFa.label: دیدگاه و شاهد
teachingAnchorsFa.text: پاسخ دیدگاه باید به موضع نویسنده تکیه کند، نه دانش بیرونی. YES موافق، NO مخالف و NOT GIVEN نامعلوم است. در خلاصه، یک واژهٔ مناسب از بند مربوط بردارید. ابتدا مستقل پاسخ دهید، سپس عنوان ردشده و حد ادعا را توضیح دهید.

locale.feedbackGuidanceFa: پس از ثبت پاسخ، دلیل خطا یا ضعف را بررسی کنید و یک اصلاح مشخص انجام دهید. این بازخورد نمرهٔ معتبر آیلتس نیست.
